title: Research: how SRS is used and what it needs

sections.name: purpose
sections.label: Purpose
sections.content: Standing research into SRS in use, kept beside the work so a story can be told from evidence rather than memory. Each thread follows one question over time: how work flows, how decisions settle, whether SRS needs a graph element, how a repository is structured for humans. A thread ends only when its question is answered by a decision or an affirmed record.

sections.name: practice
sections.label: How a thread works
sections.content:
A thread is a container titled "<question or name> (yyyy-mm-dd started)". Its anchor note holds the case so far: the claim, the story the evidence tells, the strands, and the open questions. It is rewritten as evidence arrives, never appended to as a log.

Evidence joins by declared membership: an existing record (a vignette, problem, finding, decision, strategy contract) is added to the thread, not copied. New evidence (an issue comment, a demo, a measurement) becomes a finding in Suggestions that evidences the problem or contract it bears on, and is also added to the thread. Owner words enter as vignettes in their conversation container first (Narrative explorations).

Counter-evidence goes in the same thread, marked as such. A thread that only collects support is advocacy, not research.

sections.name: find
sections.label: How to find it
sections.content: srs find --container 2f14de07-0850-4f32-9870-f241630d9537 lists every thread anchor. To search one thread: srs find --container <thread container> --text "<term>". Threads: the graph fd02df3d-5b57-46b6-80ca-beb977bf8931; human-readable repositories 02a7e2e4-bdb9-489c-8bf5-1e4aa0c01c7f; the archetypal flow 165f3a6e; flow model B b9c5106b; programme coordination by seven questions 2a13a5c7; the decision flow 68b6eb64. Each is also a child container of Research. srs-context points here (convention a752700b, in its Brief), so a session in any repository can find it.
